messages:
maya: Ran an nsys capture on the nightly runner after the kernel-selector change — seeing periodic cudaMallocAsync spikes aligned with batch flushes. timeline attached. Anyone run into allocation storms like this recently?

raj: Do we have host-side stacks + nvtx? Could be fallback from cudaMallocAsync to cudaMalloc. Perfetto or nsys output would help.

maya: Yes — timeline shows lots of small allocations (~32–128KB) every ~200ms. NVTX shows overlap between 'kv_cache::ensure_space' and 'batcher::flush_prepared'. nsys command I used: `nsys profile --output=alloc-storm --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --duration=60 ./run_profiler.sh`.

sam: Remember the kernel-selector PR (8f9a) changed the temp_workspaces: we went from stream-local pools to per-request allocation to simplify concurrency. That could increase allocation churn.

tess: Attaching a tiny excerpt from the nsys kernel timeline: ```Kernel timeline: cudaMallocAsync [host->device] spikes @ 0.2s intervals; kernels A/B/C overlapping with host memcpy; NVTX frames: kv_cache::ensure_space -> batcher::flush_prepared -> kernel_selector::choose_variant``` Also heap snapshot shows many small free slabs sitting fragmented (no coalescing).

maya: Stackshot shows: `cudaMallocAsync -> gpu_allocator::alloc_slow_path -> arena->alloc_slab` — arena seems to deplete and fall back to allocator slow path.

raj: Two quick mitigations: a) pre-reserve per-batcher scratch pools sized for peak_seq_len * shard_count and reuse; b) improve slab freelist to coalesce adjacent free chunks during reclaim. Which is easier short-term?

sam: Pre-reserve seems fastest to test. We can add an env toggle to increase slab size for a canary run. Suggested quick experiment: `export RW_ARENA_SLAB_SIZE=8388608` (8MB) and run the benchmark.

maya: Did that — malloc storms reduced dramatically but tail latency for tiny requests went up ~3–5ms. So it's a tradeoff: fewer allocations but increased internal fragmentation per-request.

tess: Another angle: change batching heuristic to pack contexts that will reuse the KV cache together (micro-LRU grouping) so we amortize allocations across similar contexts instead of scattering. Low-risk change.

maya: Collected perf samples with callgraphs: `perf record -g -F 99 -- ./run_small_load.sh` — `kv_cache::load_page` shows up as a hotspot correlated with those allocation spikes.

perf-bot: nsys capture uploaded: s3://redwood-artifacts/profiles/2070123456-alloc-storm.qdrep (contains timeline, host stacks, and heap snapshots).

raj: Found the regression root-cause candidate: commit 8f9a switched temp_workspace allocation from stream-local to request-local in kernel-selector. Proposed patch: move temp_workspace back to stream-local and reuse across requests (allocate once per CUDA stream).

sam: I'll prototype a stream-local cache for temp_workspace. If we reuse per-stream buffers we avoid allocating in the fast path and should eliminate most cudaMallocAsync calls.

maya: Quick experiment: after prototyping stream-local buffers, perfetto trace shows ~80% drop in cudaMallocAsync events. GPU occupancy dropped ~5% because fewer concurrent tiny buffers, but tail latency improved overall. Worth it.

tess: Plan of action: 1) land env slab-size toggle for a short canary, 2) prototype and test stream-local temp_workspace reuse, 3) add small batching LRU to improve KV reuse, 4) re-run nsys + NVTX on nightly load and compare. I'll own the perf regression checks.

maya: Opened RFC/PR with data + graphs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6789 — includes traces and heap diffs.

sam: Assigning infra runs to @raj and perf regression tracking to @tess. Thanks team.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled for 2027-05-12 03:00 UTC :rocket:
